description: Composite Fig. 1 with two panels of different kinds. (a) is a temperature–time (T–t) process schematic, y-axis labelled "Temperature", x-axis an unlabelled time axis; two horizontal dashed lines mark the transformation temperatures Ac3 (upper) and Ac1 (lower). The printed thermomechanical schedule runs: heating to "1 200 °C for 60 min", then "1 100 °C", finish rolling at "880 °C", "Cold rolled" (zigzag at low temperature), re-heating/annealing in the critical region at "750, 800, 850 °C for 30 min", then low-bainite aging at "400 °C for 30 min". Four inset micrographs sit along the curve showing microstructure evolution after hot rolling (banded lamellar/pearlitic structure), after cold rolling, after intercritical annealing (granular carbides in a ferrite matrix), and after aging. (b) combines a photograph of the rolled plate labelled "Thin wall structure" with a red rectangle and a yellow "RD" arrow, a superimposed line "(b) Multiphase microstructure low-density steels", a stepped specimen drawing labelled I and II with a "1.6 mm" thickness arrow, a photo of the tensile specimen, and a dimensioned tensile coupon: 14 mm gauge length, 5 mm gauge width, 1 mm thickness, 58 mm total length. Together they define the processing route and the sampling of tensile (I) and microstructure (II) specimens.

subfigures.description: Temperature–time process schematic (y-axis 'Temperature', unlabelled time axis) with dashed lines marked Ac3 and Ac1. Printed steps: '1 200 °C for 60 min', '1 100 °C', '880 °C', 'Cold rolled', '750, 800, 850 °C for 30 min', '400 °C for 30 min'. Four unlabelled inset micrographs sit at successive positions on the curve to show microstructure evolution; no scale bars are legible on the insets.

Sampling schematic/photograph: a rolled plate photo labelled 'Thin wall structure' with a red rectangle and yellow 'RD' arrow, an overlaid caption line '(b) Multiphase microstructure low-density steels', a stepped specimen geometry drawing labelled I and II (1.6 mm thickness indicated), a tensile-specimen photograph, and a dimensioned flat tensile coupon: gauge length 14 mm, width 5 mm, thickness 1 mm, overall length 58 mm, plus a 10 mm dimension.

observations.observation: Panel (a) is a temperature–time schedule; its y-axis is labelled 'Temperature' and its horizontal time axis carries no legible unit label.
Two horizontal dashed lines in (a) are labelled 'Ac3' (upper) and 'Ac1' (lower), delimiting the intercritical region used for annealing.
Printed processing steps in (a) read: '1 200 °C for 60 min', '1 100 °C', '880 °C', 'Cold rolled', '750, 800, 850 °C for 30 min' and '400 °C for 30 min'.

Four inset micrographs are placed along the (a) curve at successive process stages (after hot rolling, after cold rolling, after annealing, after aging); none carries a legible scale bar or stage label.
Panel (b) shows a photograph of the hot/cold-rolled plate annotated 'Thin wall structure', with a red rectangular region and a yellow arrow labelled 'RD' (rolling direction).
A text line overlaid in panel (b) reads '(b) Multiphase microstructure low-density steels'.
Panel (b) contains a stepped specimen outline labelled I and II with an arrow annotated '1.6 mm', plus a photograph of a dog-bone tensile specimen.
The tensile coupon drawing in (b) is dimensioned 14 mm (gauge length), 5 mm (gauge width), 1 mm (thickness) and 58 mm (overall length), with a 10 mm dimension marked on the grip section.

The caption labels a sampling schematic as '(c) Sampling schematic of tensile (I) and microstructure (II) specimens', but the supplied image contains only panels (a) and (b); the caption numbering does not match the panel letters visible in the figure.
The figure is described in the caption as showing 'Preparation process and microstructure evolution of multiphase microstructure', and the full process flow is said to be illustrated in Fig. 1(a).
The ingot was Fe-0.25C-3Mn-2Al-0.4Si-0.009S-0.009P, 39 kg, produced via vacuum induction melting; billets 90 x 70 x 40 mm were heated to 1200 °C for 60 min.
Hot rolling started at 1100 °C, involved six passes with 90% cumulative reduction to 4 mm plate thickness, finishing at 880 °C followed by air cooling.

Cold rolling used a 60% reduction to 1.6 mm thickness, followed by annealing at 750, 800, 850 °C for 30 min (AN750, AN800, AN850) and low-bainite aging at 400 °C for 30 min (AN750-T, AN800-T, AN850-T).
Tensile specimens were cut along the rolling direction to GB/T 228.1-2021 with gauge dimensions 14 mm x 5 mm x 1 mm and tested at 5 x 10^-4 s^-1 with DIC images captured every 2 s.
